sources.note: Nothing. Cites Umbugarla forms only; no Ngurmbur data.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2001. A grammar of Limilngan: a language of the Mary River region, Northern Territory, Australia. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 516, p.9
sources.note: Phonology section is for Limilngan only. On Ngurmbur (p.9): 'To the south-east, it appears that Limilngan bordered on a language known as Ngombur. This language is also extinct.. There is a little material on Ngombur, collected by Gavan Breen and Nick Evans. This material suggests that Ngombur was related to, and possibly dialectal with, its southern neighbour Umbugarla.' No Ngurmbur phonology.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 1992. The Gaagudju people and their language. PhD thesis, University of Sydney, vol. 1, introductory list of neighbouring languages, item '8. Umbugarla' (c. p.12-13)
sources.note: Stress section (5.1) is for Gaagudju only. On Ngomburr: 'This language [Umbugarla] includes Umbugarla proper and Ngomburr. It also appears that it may have included Bugurnidja (Evans: p.c.).' Also ethnographic remarks on Ngomburr/Umbugarla clan-name systems (Keen 1980). No Ngurmbur phonology. (The Mouton 2002 grammar, p.14, cited by Glottolog, is the published version of this thesis; not opened.)

Would confirm the full holdings list (recordings 1975, 1981; any AIATSIS manuscripts by Breen or Evans) and documentation scores; blocked (not reachable by automated download / DNS) by automated download.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page 'Ngurmbur' (ngur1260), Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (eds)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification 'Unattested'; comment: Ethnologue entries follow neighbours' reports of a tribe by this name (map in Harvey 2001:xii); 'only second hand meta-reports are available on the supposed language, and was said to be similar to Umbugarla [umr] (Harvey 2002:14, Davies 1989). Consequently, it cannot be asserted that Ngurmbur [nrx] was a separate language.' No descriptive references listed.
